Name: Abigail Jastal
Badge: Teacher as Researcher | Sustaining Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that I need to provide more opportunities for my students to have conversations with each other. I feel that through the conversations they had their knowledge grew far more then if I had just stood up there and talked. I also learned that my students are extremely competitive and I can use that to get them more engaged with what they are doing. The research process allowed me to take the time to think about how my lesson is being beneficial and how it could be improved.

Think back to a moment during the lesson sequence that stands out. It could be a comment from a student, an unexpected challenge or success, a shift in engagement, or a moment when your own thinking changed. Describe what happened and why this moment feels meaningful to you now. What does it reveal:
This moment was a success that occured after having gone through all the resources, the kids pared up based on their similar opinions, and I saw them having conversations about all the information they have learned. I realized that sometimes they really just need time to process before they are able to answer the complex comprehension questions I give them.
As you look over the drafts your students produced in this lesson sequence, what early patterns, surprises, or questions are emerging for you?
